==History==
Its founding origin is unknown. Originally it stood on {{ill|Mount Nijō|arz|نيجو سان|ceb|Nijō San|fr|Mont Nijō|ja|二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|lld|Mont Nijō|qid=Q11371271|lt=Mount Nijō}} and was called '''Nijō Gongen'''. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as “Shinaga Shrine, {{ill|Ishikawa district|ja|石川郡 (大阪府)|zh|石川郡 (大阪府)|qid=Q11586399|lt=Ishikawa District}}, {{ill|Kawachi Province|be|Каваты (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Kawachi|ckb|پارێزگای کاواچی|cs|Provincie Kawači|de|Provinz Kawachi|es|Provincia de Kawachi|fa|ولایت کاواچی|fr|Province de Kawachi|gl|Provincia de Kawachi|hak|Kawachi-koet|id|Provinsi Kawachi|it|Kawachi (provincia)|ja|河内国|ko|가와치국|lt|Kavačio žemė|nl|Kawachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Kawachi|ru|Кавати (провинция)|simple|Kawachi Province|sk|Kawači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Кавачи|tr|Kawachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Каваті|zh|河內國|zh_min_nan|Kawati-kok|zh_yue|河內國|qid=Q1047150}},” and ranked as a small shrine. In {{ill|Ryakunin|fa|ریاکونین|fr|Ère Ryakunin|ia|Ryakunin|id|Ryakunin|ja|暦仁|ko|랴쿠닌|ru|Рякунин|simple|Ryakunin|sr|Рјакунин|tr|Ryakunin|uk|Рякунін|zh|曆仁|qid=Q1193948}} 1 ({{ill|1238|ab|1238|af|1238|als|1238|am|1238 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1238|ar|1238|ary|1238|arz|1238|ast|1238|avk|1238|az|1238|azb|۱۲۳۸ (میلادی)|be|1238|be_x_old|1238|bg|1238|bn|১২৩৮|bpy|মারি ১২৩৮|br|1238|bs|1238.|ca|1238|cdo|1238 nièng|ceb|1238|ckb|١٢٣٨|crh|1238|cs|1238|csb|1238|cv|1238|cy|1238|da|1238|de|1238|diq|1238|el|1238|eml|1238|eo|1238|es|1238|et|1238|eu|1238|fa|۱۲۳۸ (میلادی)|fi|1238|fo|1238|fr|1238|frr|1238|fy|1238|ga|1238|gan|1238年|gcr|1238|gd|1238|gl|1238|he|1238|hi|१२३८|hr|1238.|ht|1238 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1238|hy|1238|id|1238|ilo|1238|io|1238|is|1238|it|1238|ja|1238年|jv|1238|ka|1238|kaa|1238|kk|1238 жыл|ko|1238년|la|1238|lb|1238|lij|1238|lmo|1238|lt|1238 m.|lv|1238. gads|map_bms|1238|mdf|1238|mg|1238|mhr|1238|mi|1238|min|1238|mk|1238|mr|इ.स. १२३८|mrj|1238 и|ms|1238|my|၁၂၃၈|mzn|۱۲۳۸|nap|1238|nds|1238|new|सन् १२३८|nl|1238|nn|1238|no|1238|nrm|1238|nso|1238|oc|1238|or|୧୨୩୮|os|1238-æм аз|pl|1238|pnb|1238|pt|1238|qu|1238|ro|1238|ru|1238 год|rue|1238|sa|१२३८|sah|1238|scn|1238|sd|1238ع|se|1238|sh|1238.|shn|1238|simple|1238|sk|1238|sl|1238|smn|1238|sq|1238|sr|1238|su|1238|sv|1238|sw|1238|tg|Соли 1238|th|พ.ศ. 1781|tk|1238|tl|1238|tly|1238|tr|1238|tt|1238 ел|uk|1238|ur|1238ء|uz|1238|vec|1238|vi|1238|war|1238|wuu|1238年|xmf|1238|yo|1238|zh|1238年|zh_min_nan|1238 nî|zh_yue|1238年|qid=Q5433}}), it was moved to its current location. There had originally been an Ebisu Shrine (also called Tsuchi-so Shrine) at the current site, and tradition says it became a {{ill|Massha|ja|末社|qid=Q135009906}} when Shinaga Shrine moved there.

Until the Edo period it was called '''Hassha Daimyōjin'''. ''Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku'' states: “When {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Fujiwara no Yoritaka}} moved Nijō Gongen to the current site, he invited and merged Kasuga deities, ancestral gods of the Fujiwara clan, and likely suppressed the old name Shinaga Shrine and called it Hassha Daimyōjin.”

There is also a tradition that this was the birthplace of {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803}}, and among shrine treasures is a model helmet said to have been used by her. ''Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku'' notes that “Shinaga may have shifted from Shinaga -> Isanaga -> Okinaga, giving rise to the Empress Jingū birthplace legend from the Okinaga lineage.”

It was ranked as gōsha on April 1, Meiji 5, and designated as a shinsen-heihaku offering shrine on January 28, Meiji 40. In Meiji 40, nearby Shinagaoka Shrine and Susanoo Shrine were {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|fr|Politique de consolidation des sanctuaires|ja|神社合祀|simple|Shrine Consolidation Policy|zh|神社合祀|qid=Q11590700|lt=merged}}.

==Facilities==
Precinct shrines include Nijō Shrine, Ebisu Shrine, Kotohira Shrine, and Inari Shrine.

This area was formerly the hereditary land of Soga no Kurayamada no Ishikawamaro; at the shrine front is the tomb of {{ill|Ono no Imoko|be|Она но Імока|fa|اونو نو ایموکو|fr|Ono no Imoko|ja|小野妹子|ko|오노노 이모코|ms|Ono no Imoko|pt|Ono no Imoko|ru|Оно-но Имоко|sh|Ono no Imoko|uk|Оно но Імоко|vi|Ono no Imoko|zh|小野妹子|zh_classical|小野妹子|zh_min_nan|Ono no Imoko|qid=Q1284072}}, and nearby are the mausolea of {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|ar|الإمبراطور كوتوكو|arz|الامبراطور كوتوكو|azb|کوتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Котаку|ca|Kōtoku Tennō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆتۆکو|cs|Kótoku|de|Kōtoku|es|Kōtoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور کوتوکو|fr|Kōtoku|id|Kaisar Kōtoku|it|Kōtoku|ja|孝徳天皇|ka|კოტოკუ|ko|고토쿠 천황|mr|कोतोकू|nl|Kotoku|pl|Kōtoku|pt|Kotoku|ru|Император Котоку|sh|Car Kōtoku|simple|Emperor Kōtoku|sl|Cesar Kotoku|sv|Kotoku|th|จักรพรรดิโคโตกุ|tl|Emperador Kōtoku|tr|Kōtoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Котоку|uz|Imperator Kōtoku|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōtoku|wuu|孝德天皇|yo|Emperor Kōtoku|zh|孝德天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôtoku Thian-hông|zh_yue|孝德天皇|qid=Q317980}} and {{ill|Empress Suiko|ar|الإمبراطورة سويكو|ast|Emperatriz Suiko|azb|امپراتریس سویکو|bcl|Emperatris Suiko|be|Імператрыца Суйка|ca|Suiko|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سویکۆ|cs|Suiko|de|Suiko|es|Suiko Tennō|eu|Suiko|fa|امپراتریس سوئیکو|fi|Suiko|fr|Suiko|hak|Suiko Thiên-fòng|he|סויקו, קיסרית יפן|hu|Szuiko japán császárnő|id|Suiko|it|Suiko|ja|推古天皇|ka|სუიკო|ko|스이코 천황|la|Suiko (imperatrix)|nl|Suiko|pl|Suiko|pt|Suiko|ru|Императрица Суйко|sh|Carica Suiko|simple|Empress Suiko|sl|Cesarica Suiko|sv|Suiko|ta|பேரரசி சுய்கோ|th|จักรพรรดินีซูอิโกะ|tl|Emperatris Suiko|tr|Suiko (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператор Суйко|uz|Imperator Suiko|vi|Thiên hoàng Suiko|zh|推古天皇|zh_classical|推古天皇|zh_min_nan|Suiko Thian-hông|zh_yue|推古天皇|qid=Q298057}}. Also in {{ill|Eifuku-ji|arz|ايفوكو جى|fr|Eifuku-ji|ja|叡福寺|qid=Q11410732}} in Taishi is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinaga-ryō}} (Shōtoku Taishi mausoleum; Eifukuji-kita kofun).
